primary.title: Sidereus Nuncius
primary.author: Galileo Galilei
primary.rationale: Galileo's groundbreaking report on his telescopic observations of the Moon, Jupiter's moons, and the Milky Way. It is a foundational text in the Scientific Revolution.

primary.title: Dialogo sopra i due massimi sistemi del mondo
primary.author: Galileo Galilei
primary.rationale: Galileo's famous dialogue comparing the Copernican and Ptolemaic systems, which led to his trial by the Inquisition. It is a key document in the history of science and religion.

primary.title: Discorsi e dimostrazioni matematiche intorno a due nuove scienze
primary.author: Galileo Galilei
primary.rationale: Galileo's final major work, published in exile, which laid the foundations for modern physics, particularly in kinematics and the strength of materials.

secondary.title: Galileo's Daughter: A Historical Memoir of Science, Faith, and Love
secondary.author: Dava Sobel
secondary.rationale: A highly acclaimed and accessible biography that uses Galileo's letters to his daughter to explore his life, work, and conflicts.

secondary.title: Galileo: A Very Short Introduction
secondary.author: John L. Heilbron
secondary.rationale: A concise yet comprehensive overview of Galileo's life, scientific contributions, and historical context by a leading historian of science.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Galileo
secondary.author: Nick Wilding
secondary.rationale: A collection of essays by prominent scholars covering various aspects of Galileo's life, work, and legacy, offering in-depth scholarly analysis.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources are widely available in English translation on Wikisource and Project Gutenberg, and in original Italian on Internet Archive. Secondary sources are major academic works providing scholarly context and analysis.
